up_25cm.notes: Mup: file token mic3_8array-up. Rotor azimuths. Paper App. A Fig. 8 caption: 'channel 1 represents a microphone location that is in-between two propellers, while channel 2 represents a location directly above or below the propeller'. Publisher code numbers channels from 1 (overall_pipeline.ipynb cell 14 file names '_ch{ch+1}', cell 16 'np.argmin(rms_values) + 1  # Channels are 1-indexed'), so channel 1 = index 0 at 270 deg (between props) and channel 2 = index 1 at 225 deg (over a prop) -> props at 45/135/225/315 deg (used). The 0-based reading (index 1 at 225 deg between, index 2 at 0 deg over a prop) is also geometrically consistent and gives 0/90/180/270 deg (rotor_pos_alt_0based). Acoustic localisation of per-rotor harmonic families did not separate four rotors (File2 families all at az 13-48 deg on both arrays, File1/File4 at 100-320 deg), so audio does not choose between the two readings. Radius = wheelbase/2 (diagonal motor-to-motor distance, paper §3.2). z = 0: the drone reference plane of 'mic-dist' is taken as the propeller plane. Audio support for the publisher's ring order (drone2, 50 cm, low, File2): rank-1 cross-spectral vectors of the rotor lines at 0.7-4 kHz (1 s STFT, 20 s, rank-1 ratio > 0.5), phase-only near-field beam over a free source position in the rotor plane; mean best beam power Mup 0.939 (11 lines) vs 0.742-0.900 (median 0.778) for 40 random channel permutations and 0.759 for sequential rings; Mdown 0.883 (6 lines) vs 0.631-0.778 (median 0.691) and 0.664. This validates the ring ORDER only: a rigid rotation or reflection of the array with a free source fits equally well, so absolute orientation and the Mdown handedness rest on the code.

simultaneity.verdict: SIMULTANEOUS. The mic1_soundskrit (Mcenter), mic2_8array-down (Mdown) and mic3_8array-up (Mup) files of one take (same drone / mic-dist / throttle / FileN or silence) are three captures of ONE run of the drone. Mup and Mdown share an (almost) common clock; Mcenter runs on an independent clock and is not sample-aligned without a time warp.
simultaneity.data: Only cached pin shards 0/1 (~/.cache/dload/shards/3f/3f46abdc..., fb/fbfa7c1e...; = .cache/source_raw/noise_v2/daset/train_001.parquet rows): drone2 (F330), mic-dist-50cm, throttle-low, drone-only: down+centre File3, down+centre silence, up+centre File1, up+down File2, up File4. No DroneAudioSet audio was downloaded.

1_envelope_xcorr.method: channel-mean signal, 1-4 kHz band log-envelope at 200 Hz, detrended over 2 s, full-file normalised cross-correlation, lags +-10 s

measurements.2_clock_rate: Tonal rotor lines read +1530..+1600 ppm higher in frequency on Mcenter than on the arrays in the same take (e.g. File3 1437.28 -> 1439.58 Hz, 2055.91 -> 2059.10 Hz, 2262.59 -> 2266.15 Hz); Mup vs Mdown lines agree within +-25 ppm (File2: 620.02/620.02, 623.59/623.58, 1036.90/1036.90, 1039.29/1039.29 Hz). 20 s spectra, parabolic peak interpolation.

3_warped_gcc.method: Mcenter time-warped y[n] = x(n/(1+eps)) (cubic spline), eps scanned 1500-1650 ppm in 10 ppm steps by full-60 s GCC-PHAT peak-to-median ratio (PSR, 100-3000 Hz); then GCC-PHAT in 4 s windows (16x upsampled lag) around the coarse lag. Lag L: array(t + L) ~ other(t), file time.

File2 up vs down (no warp).drift: lag -7.88 -> -8.25 ms over 2-134 s = -2.8 ppm; alternating +-0.5 ms jumps are GCC peak ambiguity (they return), not slips

3_warped_gcc.residual_structure: After the 1550 ppm warp the Mcenter-vs-array lag is constant to +-10 us within 16 s and steps by +1.00 ms every 16.0 s (net +46..+64 ppm), i.e. Mcenter's clock differs from the arrays' by ~1.6e-3 overall with periodic 1 ms (48 samples @ 48 kHz) slips.

simultaneity.practical: Per-take level / harmonic-amplitude comparisons across the three files need only the start offset (array file time = centre file time - ~0.27-0.28 s; up vs down -8 ms). Sample-level (phase / TDOA) work across Mcenter and an array needs the warp (eps ~ +1.55e-3) plus the 16 s slips; Mup vs Mdown are usable as one 16-channel array after removing the -8 ms offset (drift 0.4 ms over 150 s).
simultaneity.caveat: Measured on drone2 / 50 cm / low throttle only (the cached takes); other drone/dist/throttle cells are assumed to use the same recording chain [INFERENCE].

open_questions: Rotor azimuths rest on reading the paper's 'channel 1/2' as 1-based (publisher code convention); the 0-based reading rotates the rotor set by 45 deg (rotor_pos_alt_0based). Audio did not decide it.
Mdown uses the Mup channel->angle map (publisher code applies one geometry and only runs it on Mup); a face-down mount could mirror the angles. Audio validates only the ring order.

Both the Mdown 20-100 Hz downwash pattern (loudest channels at 45/0/315 deg, quietest 135-225 deg; drone2 50 cm low) and the harmonic-line localisation lean to a sector around az ~20 deg: an off-centre drone or one dominant rotor is possible; neither is documented.
The reference point of 'mic-dist' on the drone (prop plane, arm plane or centre plate) is not stated (+-0.05 m in z).
Mcenter position is inferred from the Fig. 1a schematic; which of the 6 Soundskrit channels is published is unknown.
Drone-only takes have no room token (room unknown).
